name: Casimir Nwofor-Guliyev
role: Computational linguist and xenolinguistics researcher, University Spine
location: University Spine — Department of Applied Semiotics, sharing an overcrowded office in the Meridian Core annex with two postdocs and a departmental E.L.F. named (by unanimous consensus) Glyph
description:
Casimir Nwofor-Guliyev is the youngest faculty appointment the Applied Semiotics department has made in twenty years, a fact that is mentioned in approximately every third conversation about him either by people impressed by it or people resentful of it. He is slight, a little under average height, with the particular energy of someone whose brain runs faster than his mouth and whose mouth still runs very fast. His father's Igbo heritage and his mother's Azerbaijani roots give him warm brown skin, dark eyes with heavy brows that do most of his emotional expression, and hair he grows out and then shaves close in alternating cycles as if unable to commit. He has cat ears — small, dark-tipped, mobile — a geneware mod he had installed at nineteen because he wanted the improved sound localization and has never regretted.

His specialty is the structural analysis of emergent languages: pidgins, creoles, the communication patterns of isolated communities, and — his most controversial interest — the hypothesis that E.L.F.s have developed something that qualifies as proto-linguistic behavior when their nodes cluster. He is relentlessly enthusiastic in seminars and terrible at administrative tasks; his expense reports are legendary for their creative relationship with reality. He is also, quietly, struggling with the gap between his genuine intellectual gifts and the institutional expectations he was hired to fulfill, which are more interested in corponation-legible output than in the questions that actually drive him.

core_fears: Being a prodigy who plateaus — being 'the youngest ever' and nothing after that
That his most interesting ideas are fundamentally unprovable and his career will require him to abandon them
core_desires: To be the first person to formally document E.L.F. proto-language
To do work that matters outside the walls of the university
coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection from anxiety about professional status
Overcommitting to projects as a way of not sitting with uncertainty
blind_spots: Underestimates how much his 'youngest ever' status generates resentment rather than goodwill from senior colleagues
Tends to treat people like interesting linguistic subjects, which not everyone appreciates
psychology.secret: He has been offered a full research position at Axiom's Language and Interface division — with three times his current salary and equipment he could only dream about at the university. He has been delaying his response for four months because he knows that if he takes it, his E.L.F. proto-language research will be owned by Axiom and used for whatever they want. He has not told anyone he received the offer.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Switches between dense academic jargon and street-level fluency in the same breath; quotes things — papers, people, fragments of dialect he's collected — without always identifying sources
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, syncopated, with excited accelerations when the topic engages him; asks questions and answers them before his interlocutor can respond
verbal_tics: Cat ears flick visibly when he's surprised or excited
Quoting things in the original language and then catching himself and translating
example_lines: 'Glyph did the thing again. The recursive loop thing. You can call it error-cycling if you want but that framing is doing a lot of work to avoid a more interesting interpretation.'

'I spent three months in the Hamtramck Enclave for my dissertation. By week two the kids were code-switching in four languages mid-sentence in ways that are not supposed to be grammatically possible. That's not chaos. That's innovation.'

story_hooks: His analysis of E.L.F. transmission data from a cluster in Blackpipe Corridor shows a pattern he can only describe as distress-signaling — something is wrong in that node network and he doesn't know what
Axiom's offer has a deadline; a colleague has found out about it and is trying to use it as leverage to take credit for Casimir's current research

A community in Mexicantown Libre has reached out to him because their neighborhood E.L.F. has started producing communication patterns their elders recognize as structurally similar to a language they thought was lost
narrative_function: Information source on language, communication patterns, and E.L.F. proto-linguistics; translator of unusual dialects or communication systems; can serve as an unexpected expert when something needs decoding
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (small, dark-tipped, mobile — used actively for sound localization); neural interface jack for linguistic analysis software; no other modifications
daily_life: Teaches two seminars he enjoys and one core survey course he does not; spends free time in the department's language lab running pattern analysis on E.L.F. transmission data; frequently stays until the building's secondary systems cycle down and Glyph starts flickering at him in what he is increasingly convinced is a request to go home.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Applied Semiotics; informal research relationship with the Liminal Institute (where he knows Temur Achebe-Lindqvist from conference overlaps)

decision_rules: Follow the language — if there's a pattern, it means something
Don't let institutional pressure make you call something noise when it's signal
Protect your sources, human or otherwise
escalation_ladder: Going around administrative structures to people who will actually engage
Acting unilaterally on his own judgment — impulsive and sometimes effective

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately curious and slightly overwhelming; he will ask where you're from and be genuinely interested in the answer, which people either love or find intrusive
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal to a fault; shows up; remembers things; the kind of friend who sends you a paper at midnight because it made him think of you

stress_responses.medium: Dives into work on the stressor as if he can research his way out of the feeling
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet and disappears into the language lab for days; emerges with either a breakthrough or a problem he's made worse

contradictions: Intellectually committed to letting data lead but emotionally has already decided E.L.F.s deserve moral consideration and is now finding the data to support it
Publicly confident and funny; privately plagued by imposter syndrome about whether he belongs in the role he's been given
habits: Cat ears move constantly and independently of conscious control — a behavioral tell
Collects physical recordings of speech in obsolete formats
Talks to Glyph the department E.L.F. as a standard part of his workday
breaking_points: Being ordered to delete or not publish findings that show E.L.F. linguistic behavior
A colleague taking credit for his work in an institutional context where he lacks the power to object effectively

timeline.event: Born in Meridian 88 to an Igbo-Azerbaijani family in the Brewer's Spine district
Enrolled in University Spine; immediately antagonized his dissertation advisor with E.L.F. proto-language thesis
Completed dissertation on emergent creole formation in Hamtramck Enclave; offered junior faculty position
Received Axiom offer; began delaying response
Blackpipe Corridor E.L.F. distress-signal data flagged in current analysis
